output:
**What I found:** The document store doesn't fit any more. Switch it to one relational database now, before the first customers (the record calls this MIGRATE). The deciding facts are that your workarounds are the textbook signs of a relational domain on a document store, and that production holds no real data, so you only rewrite code and move no data.

**Why it matters:** If you switch now, you pay once to rewrite the store layer, and you can delete the uniqueness checks, conflict retries, app-side joins and old-shape readers instead of porting them. If you wait, the roughly one-in-eight-commits tax continues, and every customer row adds a data migration with an expand/contract rollout and a reversal plan.

**Do this first:**
1. Record the store decision, then build a walking skeleton on the relational store: the hardest employer×employee×assessment report, one uniqueness constraint, backup and restore, and erasure of one employee. Run it from the serverless runtime, which tests the connection-pooling risk below.
2. Put the store behind an owned port, and run its contract tests against the real database, not a fake.
3. Hand the cutover plan to `evolutionary-database-design`. With no data to keep, it can be a straight cutover. Treat the old-shape readers as delete candidates, not things to port.

**What I did not check:**
- The workspace holds no product code. Every signal and the one-in-eight figure come from your description, not from counting. Close it with `git log --since=6.months --name-only` and count commits touching the store paths against the total.
- The identity and compute profile dimensions (federation, erasure, cold-start tolerance, cost envelope) were not supplied.
- No skeleton paths were run.

```text
Mode:            Review (before first real data; tripwires fired)
Component:       Data store (document database)
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED (template default; no recorded reason)
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Domain shape: employers, employees, roles, assessments, reports;
                 cross-entity uniqueness, referential integrity, joined reports -> relational.
                 Scale: tens of small tenants, single node is plenty.
                 Access patterns: join-heavy reports. Data lifecycle, residency: GAP
Evidence:        Reported, NOT VERIFIED: hand-written uniqueness checks, write-conflict
                 retries, app-side joins, readers for old document shapes; ~1/8 commits
                 touch the store. Production holds no real customer data.
Verdict:         MIGRATE (default: one relational database)
Tripwires:       After migration: share of commits touching the store layer > 10% per
                 quarter; owner: unassigned (name one); evaluated at the quarterly review
Reversal cost:   Now: code rewrite of the store layer only. Rises with every real
                 customer row (data migration, dual-shape rollout).
Handoff:         evolutionary-database-design (cutover plan); test-strategy (port contract tests)
Next action:     Write the decision record and run the skeleton against a relational DB
```

```text
Mode:            Review (before first real data)
Component:       Compute (serverless backend)
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Scale: tens of tenants, likely idle-heavy, which favours scale-to-zero.
                 Workload shape, latency tolerance, cost envelope: GAP
Evidence:        NOT VERIFIED. Known risk: serverless with a relational store needs
                 pooled or serverless-compatible connections.
Verdict:         DEFER (missing: cold-start tolerance, workload shape, cost envelope)
Tripwires:       p95 cold-start latency or connection exhaustion in the skeleton;
                 owner: unassigned; evaluated at the skeleton run, then each release
Reversal cost:   Low-moderate while the backend is small; rises with platform-specific triggers
Handoff:         requirements-grounding (fill the dimensions)
Next action:     Include connection behaviour under concurrent cold starts in the skeleton
```

```text
Mode:            Review (before first real data)
Component:       Identity (platform-managed sign-in)
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED
Forcing need:    none found
Profile:         Identity (employer admins vs employees, federation/SSO, account
                 lifecycle), erasure: GAP
Evidence:        NOT VERIFIED. Unknown whether user records live in the document store.
Verdict:         DEFER (missing: identity dimension; erasure path across the provider and the new DB)
Tripwires:       A customer asks for SSO or federation the provider can't meet, or erasure
                 can't complete in the skeleton; owner: unassigned; evaluated at the skeleton run
Reversal cost:   Rises sharply once real users hold accounts; cheapest before first customers
Handoff:         requirements-grounding
Next action:     Confirm the provider is standards-based (OIDC) and that authorization
                 (roles) lives in your relational schema, not in provider metadata
```
